newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Royal, Scotia banks in takeover moves.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Royal, Scotia banks in takeover moves.

text.p: Two of Canada's big six banks took steps on Tuesday to tighten their grip on insurance and trust company business.
Bank of Nova Scotia said it offered to acquire Toronto-based National Trustco Co. in a cash and stock deal valued at C$1.25 billion ($898 million).
Meanwhile, one of Canada's biggest insurers, London Insurance Group, said it was in talks to be acquired by Canada's biggest bank, Royal Bank of Canada.
The announcement by London Insurance and its 58 percent-owner Trilon Financial Corp. came after the talks were reported on Tuesday in Toronto's Globe and Mail newspaper.
The companies said any agreement was expected to include an offer to all London Insurance shareholders. Citing confidentiality agreements, they said they would not comment further at this time.
Scotiabank said it would offer 0.125 of a common share plus C$26.475 ($19.04) in cash for each common share of National Trustco.

The bank said it already owned 2.4 percent of National Trustco and obtained lockup agreements for 47 percent of the company's outstanding common shares. The offer would be available to shareholders until July 31.

National Trustco chairman Hal Jackman told a news conference that the company, one of Canada's last major family-held trust companies, was not open to competing bids. Trust companies are similar to U.S. savings and loans.
"We see the acquisition of National Trust as an excellent fit strategically for both institutions," Scotiabank Chief Executive Peter Godsoe said in a statement.
